subject: general
question: A car travels 60 km in the first hour, 80 km in the second hour, and 100 km in the third hour. What is the average speed of the car over the 3 hours?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Average Speed** for equal time intervals = Arithmetic Mean of individual speeds.

Speeds are 60 km/hr, 80 km/hr, and 100 km/hr.

Average = (60 + 80 + 100) ÷ 3 = 240 ÷ 3 = 80 km/hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 80 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Distance in 1st hour (d₁) = 60 km, Time (t₁) = 1 hr

Distance in 2ⁿd hour (d₂) = 80 km, Time (t₂) = 1 hr

Distance in 3rd hour (d₃) = 100 km, Time (t₃) = 1 hr

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0bf181e11ffe72a2fbb2644d2e43303452c0df339022ee2e2bf787907ad7e670.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Distance = 60 + 80 + 100 = 240 km

⇒ Total Time = 1 + 1 + 1 = 3 hours

⇒ Average Speed = 240 ÷ 3

⇒ Average Speed = 80 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 80 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Harmonic Mean for Equal Distances

If a car covers two equal distances at speeds v₁ and v₂, the average speed is (2 × v₁ × v₂) ÷ (v₁ + v₂).

Relative Speed

When two objects move in the same direction, relative speed is |v₁ − v₂|. In opposite directions, it is (v₁ + v₂).

Unit Conversion

To convert km/hr to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/hr, multiply by 18/5.</p
